title: Regional residency policy broker and provenance exporter for private deployments
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) need a deterministic, policy-driven way to bind requests and persisted artifacts to approved regions, plus an auditable provenance export that proves residency and retention policy compliance. Current controls are scattered (routing, node-affinity, manual snapshots) and do not produce a single verifiable evidence bundle for audits or contractual attestation.

Goal: Implement a 'Residency Policy Broker' that evaluates per-tenant residency requirements (region whitelist, allowed fallback lanes, retention windows) and enforces them at request routing and storage layers, plus a 'Provenance Exporter' that packages time-ordered evidence (routing decisions, KV lease metadata, retention settings, snapshot hashes, policy version) into a signed export for compliance reviewers. The feature must support private VPC and on-prem clusters, work offline for air-gapped customers, and integrate with existing audit pipelines.

Scope: 
- Residency policy model and storage (policy versions per tenant).
- Runtime admission integration: route decision hook and node assignment enforcement.
- Retention setting propagation to storage subsystems and snapshotter.
- Provenance exporter that composes an immutable evidence bundle and signs it with KMS/HSM (or local key when air-gapped).
- Backwards compatible failover constraints that prevent automatic switchover to disallowed regions and provide graceful evacuation guidance.
- Expose export scheduling and on-demand export endpoints for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Policies can be created/updated via Console API and stored with versioning and effective timestamps
Runtime route decisions consult the Residency Policy Broker and reject or reroute requests that violate tenant policies (simulated tests pass)
Retention windows specified in policy are applied to snapshotter and object lifecycle configuration
Provenance Exporter produces a signed bundle containing policy version, decision logs for a configurable time window, snapshot hashes, and retention settings
Export bundle validates with a verifier tool and includes KMS-backed signature; air-gapped flow supports local key signing with documented caveats
Failover control prevents automatic evacuation into forbidden regions and surfaces human-approved fallback lanes in Console
Automated end-to-end test demonstrating a region outage with enforced policy that triggers allowed fallback only and emits a provenance bundle
Documentation and runbook added to private-deployments > residency folder and PR reviewed by security and compliance
design_notes: Broker model: immutable policy objects stored in etcd with an index by tenant + environment; a lightweight cache in each node for fast lookup
Decision enforcement points: API gateway (pre-routing), scheduler (node affinity), and snapshotter (persistence TTLs)
Provenance format: newline-delimited JSON log entries + tarball of snapshot metadata; bundle metadata includes policy vX hash and signature header
Signing strategy: use customer KMS when configured; fallback to node-local key for air-gapped installs with explicit warning recorded in bundle
Trade-offs: Strong enforcement at scheduler improves guarantees but complicates emergency evacuation; mitigate with an approval flow and time-limited overrides recorded in exported evidence
Privacy: decision logs in bundle must be redacted per tenant request; provide opt-in detail level for exports to balance audit needs and privacy
implementation_plan: Week 1: Schema for policy and exporter metadata, proto for decision RPCs; add API endpoints for policy CRUD
Week 2: Implement broker service with etcd persistence and local node cache; unit tests for policy versioning
Week 3: Integrate decision hook into API gateway and scheduler; add circuit to block illegal routes
Week 4: Snapshotter retention propagation and lifecycle config integration; storage adapter changes
Week 5: Build Provenance Exporter, KMS signing integration, and verifier tool
Week 6: E2E test harness (simulated region outage), documentation, security review, and canary rollout to internal staging
Post-release: Observability tweaks, performance tuning for broker cache, and operator-runbook updates
test_plan: Unit tests for policy CRUD and version conflict resolution
Integration tests: broker + API gateway to ensure blocked requests return 403 with policy reason
Fault-injection: simulate kube-node isolation and verify scheduler prevents assignment into banned regions
E2E compliance test: generate export bundle and run verifier to assert signature validity and included artifacts
Privacy test: export redaction levels and consent toggles verified against sample tenants
Load test: cache hit/miss behavior under 5k qps to ensure latency < 6ms per decision in worst-case
monitoring_and_alerting: Cache miss ratio alert if > 5% sustained over 10m
Exporter failure alert when signed bundle generation fails or KMS rejects signing
Policy drift monitor: mismatch between broker policy and node-applied affinity > 0 triggers P1
Audit export success rate and average time to generate bundle
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy broker and exporter to staging-priv with feature flag off
Stage 2: Enable export-only mode for selected internal tenants (no enforcement) to validate evidence accuracy
Stage 3: Canary enforcement for non-production tenants with manual approval flow enabled
Stage 4: Gradually enable enforcement for customer tenants who signed residency SLAs after targeted validation
Stage 5: Full rollout with operator-runbook and optional emergency override audit path
